correctness.rationale: For all integers k>=3, n>=2k+1, and 0<epsilon<1/2, the proof reduces distinct edge-pair distances to four endpoint-path affine functions. It proves each diameter bound, classifies supports by their shared elements, exactly computes area epsilon, epsilon^2, or 2epsilon^2, and counts partners via exceptional/core positions. The case of coinciding edges has maximum 1 and is outside the claimed upper tails. All quantifiers, strict inequalities and cutoff ranges are handled. The standalone exact rational checker enumerated complete edge orbits for multiple parameters and passed, but those finite tests are only corroboration.

value.rationale: A diameter is a worst-case scalar and says nothing about the probability of distances near that scalar. For natural Johnson/hypersimplex unit-edge networks of arbitrarily large vertex diameter k>=3, the exact near-diameter probability undergoes a genuine order-of-vanishing transition at the first admissible increase of ground-set size. The geometry changes from a one-dimensional ridge of farthest pairs to isolated midpoint configurations, giving distinct transport-tail behavior. The fact is exact across infinite families and a nonzero epsilon interval, not an arbitrary finite lookup or a known diameter corollary.
